# Debasish Pattanayak

> Assistant Professor, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology, Indore. Research on distributed algorithms for mobile agents and mobile robots.

I am an Assistant Professor in Computer Science and Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology, Indore. My research focuses on distributed algorithms for mobile agents and mobile robots in graphs and geometric spaces, with interests in exploration, rendezvous, dispersion, pattern formation, and fault tolerance. I also develop interactive simulators for these systems. Before joining IIT Indore, I completed my PhD in Theoretical Computer Science from the Department of Mathematics at IIT Guwahati under the supervision of Prof. Partha Sarathi Mandal and Dr. H. Ramesh, and held visiting and postdoctoral research positions in Europe and Canada. See my CV for a fuller academic profile.

My research interests lie in the design and analysis of algorithms for mobile agents and mobile robots operating in both discrete (graphs) and continuous spaces. I focus on fundamental problems such as exploration, search, rendezvous, evacuation, and filling under constraints of limited memory, communication, or environmental knowledge. I am particularly interested in distributed coordination, fault-tolerant behavior, and the impact of structure and complexity on algorithmic performance. My work spans deterministic and randomized strategies, with applications in swarm robotics, multi-agent coordination, and autonomous systems. I also work on developing simulators for these systems, a couple of them are linked here, under CCM Model and LCM Model.

## Projects

- [Mobility Matters](https://drdebmath.github.io/mobility-matters/): A Living Survey of Open Problems on Autonomous Agents, Robots and Particles ([PDF](https://drdebmath.github.io/mobility-matters/mobility-matters.pdf))
- [The Oblivious Robot](https://drdebmath.github.io/blog/): blog
- [CCM Model](https://drdebmath.github.io/CCMModel/): Interactive simulator for the coordinated concurrent movement model.
- [LCM Model](https://drdebmath.github.io/LCMmodel/): Interactive simulator for the classic Look-Compute-Move model.
- [Black Hole Search](https://drdebmath.github.io/BlackHoleSearch/): Interactive simulator for the Black Hole Search problem with Byzantine agents.
- [SILBOT](https://drdebmath.github.io/SILBOT/): Interactive simulator for the SILBOT mobile robot model.
- [MobileAutomata](https://drdebmath.github.io/MobileAutomata/): Interactive simulator for the MobileAutomata model.
- [India Future Mobility Planner](https://drdebmath.github.io/Transport/): Interactive simulator of flight vs high-speed rail vs hybrid city-center journeys.
- [Algorithm Visualizations](https://drdebmath.github.io/visualizations/): Step-by-step demos by category: traversal, shortest paths, spanning trees, online algorithms, and distributed agents.

## Research themes

- Dispersion of Mobile Agents: Time-efficient dispersion of mobile agents on anonymous graphs under asynchrony and limited communication.
- Pattern Formation by Robot Swarms: Universal pattern formation, dancing, and geometric arrangements by luminous and oblivious robots.
- Fault Tolerance & Dangerous Environments: Coordination and exploration under crash faults, Byzantine companions, and hazardous environments.
- Graph Algorithms & Mobile Computation: Leader election, connectivity, treasure hunt, and computation via mobile agents on graphs.
